Difficulty: In the same chapter God says, 'It repenteth me that I have set up Saul to be king,' and Samuel then declares that 'the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent.' Readers ask how both can be true, and whether God changes His mind.
Explanations: The standard explanation is that Scripture speaks of God in human terms when it describes His grief and His changed dealings with a person whose conduct has changed. God's settled purpose and character do not change; what changes is the relationship and the outcome, because Saul has changed. 'Repent' in verse 11 describes God's sorrow and His reversal of Saul's kingship; 'will not repent' in verse 29 denies that God is fickle or can be talked out of His settled judgment, as a man might be.
SiteAssessment: Site assessment: The two verses speak at different levels: God grieves and responds to human change, and God does not waver like a man. There is no contradiction once the human language of verse 11 is read as Scripture itself glosses it in verse 29.
